subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be denied every parent, reset target, or explicit target whose persisted pluginOwnerId is absent, with no runtime compatibility fallback for legacy ownerless rows?
rationale: Ownerless rows cannot be safely attributed to a plugin, so code cannot infer an authorized owner; exact equality closes the disclosure boundary but intentionally stops legacy plugin workflows that relied on those rows.

options.title: Confirm fail-closed equality
options.body: Keep exact owner equality, treat ownerless rows as operator-only, and require cross-store regression proof before landing.

options.title: Add explicit ownership recovery
options.body: Pause merge and design an operator-controlled doctor or claim flow that assigns ownership without allowing plugins to self-adopt ownerless rows.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow plugin runtimes to use ownerless rows and explicitly accept that the original cross-plugin isolation boundary remains incomplete.

recommendation.title: Confirm fail-closed equality
recommendation.body: Keep exact owner equality, treat ownerless rows as operator-only, and require cross-store regression proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and live routing point most strongly to this person for the session-lifecycle and security-boundary decision.
